technical_and_design_decisions: Implementation continues in Go within the existing fabric-config project structure and follows its current code style, error handling patterns, and naming conventions.
New functions are added as additional methods on existing types; SetConfiguration/GetConfiguration and SetMSP/GetMSP are kept for backward compatibility alongside the new individual setters.
For U5, consenter removal requires an exact match on all four fields (host, port, client_tls_cert, server_tls_cert) to avoid silent partial matches.

For U3, genesis block creation is updated to omit the top-level OrdererAddresses field and instead require each orderer org to specify its endpoints (required at org level when creating, optional when updating).

The CLI tool (U6) is delivered as a new command binary (e.g., cmd/configtx) following Go CLI best practices (urfave/cli or cobra) and uses the Hyperledger Fabric Gateway client SDK to submit config update transactions.
Certificate validation in U8 leverages the standard crypto/x509 package to verify PEM-encoded certificates and ensure no malformed material enters the config tree.
The CLI tool's JSON I/O uses the standard encoding/json package; the connection profile follows the documented Fabric connection-profile format.
Unit tests follow the existing table-driven style in the fabric-config repo and reuse existing test fixtures where applicable.
Discovery service is used by the CLI tool to fetch the latest config block for each channel when no explicit block is supplied.
Dry-run mode in the CLI tool writes the rendered config update envelope to stdout in a human-readable form so it can be redirected to a file.
assumptions: The developer is familiar with the existing fabric-config codebase and the Hyperledger Fabric configtx model.
Existing test helpers and channel/orderer fixtures can be reused for the new unit tests.
Hyperledger Fabric Gateway SDK is available (or added as a dependency) for the CLI tool's transaction submission and discovery calls.
Signing identities in the CLI tool are supplied as base64-encoded PEM private keys and certificates grouped by mspId.
Connection profiles are valid Fabric connection profile JSON documents including peers, orderers, organizations, and certificate authorities.
A discovery service is reachable for the target network and is used to fetch config blocks when needed.
Examples in the spec refer to the existing fabric-config examples directory; the work only extends or amends those examples rather than creating a new repo.
Unit testing effort is included inside each activity estimate; no separate QA phase is required.
A single developer performs the entire increment sequentially on one feature branch.
No large-scale refactoring of the existing configtx package is needed beyond the minimum changes required to support the new APIs.
Backward compatibility is preserved for any exported function whose signature is modified (e.g., U2 uses an options struct or variadic argument so existing callers continue to compile).
